request.spec:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show a rate calendar: for each grade and each month of the sheet's today's calendar year, the
rate in force on the first day of that month (n/a when none).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the rate calendar, but `bin/e2e` still fails 2 of its 4 tests. Both failures come from a defect in the spec, which I'm not allowed to edit.

**The change:** it's front end only, in `src/main/frontend/features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`. The Rates panel now has a table with one row per grade and one column per month of the year that the sheet's "today" falls in. Each cell, `rate-month-<grade>-<yyyy>-<mm>`, shows the rate in force on the 1st of that month, or `n/a` if none applies. It uses the same rate lookup as `rate-current-<grade>`, so a rate's start and end dates are handled the same way in both places. No server or database change was needed, since the rates were already loaded on the page.

**Test results** (`PORT=3017 bin/e2e`):
- **Pass:** "rate calendar" and "scenario 3".
- **Fail:** "scenario 1" and "scenario 2", on `sheet-parent` at lines 224 and 549. They expect the literal text `__SHEET__-p`, but the screen correctly shows the real sheet id, e.g. `smvkphovsyx0n-p`. The sheet id was apparently never filled in where the spec was written. No correct app can pass these lines as written; they should probably use `` `${sheet}-p` `` like the rest of the spec.
- **Checked with a fix:** I ran a temporary copy of the spec with that one string corrected, and all 4 tests passed, including the calendar checks after those lines. I've deleted the copy; the real spec is unchanged.

**Port 3002 is taken:** your shell sets `PORT=3002`, and a leftover Java app started at 06:35 (PID 990954, probably another sandbox's) is still running on that port. On my first run, our app couldn't start and the tests ran against that old app instead, so every action was refused. I didn't stop it because I can't tell whose it is, and ran on port 3017 instead. Until it's stopped, run the tests with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e` or another free port.

In one run, scenario 1 also had a holiday refused that went through on the next run. That looks like a one-off while the machine was busy and is unrelated to this change.
